issues.issue: Panel (b), breast cancer subplot: the y tick labels are removed, but its y range differs from the digits subplot (its ticks sit at different heights). A reader cannot read accuracy there, and the shared-looking layout invites a false visual comparison of the two gaps.
issues.fix: Give the breast cancer subplot its own y tick labels (e.g. 80, 90, 100) on its left spine, or put both subplots on one shared y range (about 60 to 100). If the ranges stay different, say so in the caption, which already says it, and keep the tick labels visible.

issues.issue: Panel (b) gap bracket is cramped. It is a thin box at x=42 to 45, and the 'NN% of gap won' text sits directly under it. In breast cancer the text spills past the axes toward the (c) 'points' label and crosses the sd band edge. The bracket also does not clearly contain the filter: only a short purple tick marks it. The brief asked for the filter to sit inside the bracket.
issues.fix: Widen the right margin (xlim up to about 60) so the bracket is at least twice as wide. Put the '68% of gap won' text beside or above the bracket, not under it, in one line or two short ones. Draw the filter marker or a purple ring inside the bracket. Keep all text inside the axes.

issues.issue: Panel (a): the '50%' label is drawn on top of the light recall bar at 40% breast cancer, and it is too small to read. The brief asked for the label 'half of drops', so the reference line's meaning is lost.
issues.fix: Move the label to the empty left margin or the top-left of the axes, above the bars, e.g. 'half of drops' in gray at x just right of the y axis with a white background patch. Keep the line behind the bars.

issues.issue: Panel (a) uses slate blue and light blue for precision and recall. The spec and the project rules reserve purple #4E2A84 and #B6ACD1 for our method. Precision and recall belong to our filter, and slate blue is a new hue that could be read as another baseline. Panel (c) then uses light purple for 'samples dropped', a different quantity, which makes the color mapping inconsistent across panels.
issues.fix: Follow the spec: precision in #4E2A84 and recall in #B6ACD1 in panel (a). In panel (c) keep the accuracy-change bars in #4E2A84 and use a lavender or gray-lavender outline or hatch for 'samples dropped' so the two light purples do not carry different meanings. Update the caption colors to match.

issues.issue: Panel (c) has its own y scale (-1.2 to 0.4 points) with no link to panel (b). The roughly 0.2-point loss looks as large as the 25-point drops in (b), and nothing in the figure says that the scale is magnified. The 'points' label and the repeated '% dropped' label next to a panel title ('samples dropped') are redundant. The panel is also sparse.
issues.fix: Add a short in-axes note such as 'zoomed scale' or put it in the caption. Replace the rotated y-labels with one clear label, e.g. 'filter minus logistic regression (points)', and drop the duplicated '% dropped' label (keep the tick unit). Label the zero line. Consider a smaller second axis so that (c) stays compact.

issues.issue: The figure has no spoken takeaway at a glance. The eye goes to the MLP collapsing in (b), not to the filter winning. The question each panel answers ('Does disagreement find flips?', 'Does dropping them help?', 'What does it cost when labels are clean?') is not visible, and the letters (a), (b), (c) are placed at inconsistent heights and distances from their panels, with (b) crowding the legend.
issues.fix: Add a small sans-serif lead-in next to each panel letter that names the question, as the brief intends (no titles inside axes, but a short line beside the letter is fine). Align the three letters on one baseline at the left edge of their panels, and move the (b) legend so it does not touch the letter. Keep the filter line the thickest and make the MLP line thinner or lighter.

issues.issue: Fonts render in a serif face, while the brief asks for a plain sans-serif in regular weight, and the other diagrams in the paper will use sans labels.
issues.fix: Set font.family to a sans-serif (e.g. DejaVu Sans or Arial/Helvetica) in the style helper or the script.

strengths: Three-panel flow from 'finds flips' to 'wins back accuracy' to 'costs nothing on clean labels' matches the planned message.
Our filter is clearly distinct in thick purple and the MLP is visibly the weakest at high noise.
Error bars and bands are present (sd over 5 seeds, 95% paired interval), and the clean-label reference line is clear.
Honest reporting: breast cancer recovery (22%) is shown next to digits (68%), and the clean-label interval that nearly excludes zero is visible.
Panel baselines are aligned and legends sit above the axes, not over the data.
